posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

Back in 2018, Philipp Dettmer, the founder of kurzgesagt, was being treated for a stage 3 B testicular cancer. This was a very serious situation, but it is not a sad story! In fact, going through chemotherapy was one of the most interesting experiences of his life. He was treated with Cisplatin, which, in a nutshell, put his body through a controlled medical violence. This toxic chemotherapy agent is a hero and a villain of this story, but it absolutely saved his life.

recentPosts.caption:
Some friendships are just too wholesome. ⁠
Pandora and her owner sharing their little moment of the day and honestly, we could watch this reunion on repeat. ⁠
⁠
She has completely stolen our hearts. ❤️⁠
🎥: @itsthatfarmguy

A whole different side of Egyptian cuisine, served straight from the Siwa Oasis. ⁠
From earthy, freshly baked bread and local-style molokheya to comforting slow-cooked dishes, Siwi food has its own distinct character and traditions.⁠
⁠
And honestly, the food alone makes the journey to this desert oasis even more tempting.⁠
🎥: @alexploringlife

In South Africa’s Kruger National Park, a train has been turned into a hotel and permanently parked on a bridge above the Sabie River.⁠
⁠
It’s called Kruger Shalati, and it was inspired by the park’s early days in the 1920s, when the first visitors traveled by train and stopped overnight on this very bridge. Today, guests sleep in carriage rooms and can watch wildlife gather along the river from the pool deck.⁠
⁠
Would you spend a night on this train hotel? ⁠
⁠
By: @kruger_shalati

Not your average mountain hike… and definitely not for anyone who hates tight spaces! 😅⛰️⁠
⁠
Hidden in New Hampshire, this trail takes you through narrow caves and rocky passages where a little squeezing is part of the adventure. It’s challenging, unexpected and easily one of the most unique hiking experiences you can have in the U.S.⁠
⁠
Would you dare to take this one on?⁠
⁠
🎥: @thelopezadventure

Thousands of olive ridley sea turtles came ashore on Costa Rica’s Pacific coast to lay their eggs, turning the entire beach into a sea of shells.⁠
⁠
This mass nesting event is called an “arribada,” Spanish for “arrival.” ⁠
⁠
Over just a few nights, huge numbers of female turtles arrive together to nest, and Costa Rica is one of the best places in the world to see it.⁠
⁠
By: @dionisio_castro_foto

Meet two little guinea pigs with a very serious talent for being adorable💛⁠
⁠
From fluffy bee hoods to tiny flower hats, they always seem ready for a photoshoot, and they’ve even got a collection of plush friends that look just like them.⁠
⁠
By: @chu_yuk_yuen

Ready to put your courage and climbing skills to the test? 😅🏔️⁠
Challenge Trails at Shanghai Disney is one of those experiences you don’t expect to find in a theme park and definitely one worth trying! ⁠
⁠
Each obstacle comes with three difficulty levels, so you can choose your challenge depending on how adventurous you’re feeling.⁠
A little thrill, a lot of fun, and a whole new way to explore the park!⁠
🎥: @via.kat

This incredible ribbon lightning happens when a single lightning bolt strikes several times in a row through the same path, while strong winds push that path sideways between each strike. ⚡⁠
⁠
The camera captures every strike side by side, creating this ribbon-like effect.⁠
⁠
Have you ever seen lightning like this?⁠
⁠
By: @kane_mclatchie_photography

In Bosnia, coffee comes with a little extra ritual. ☕🚬⁠
A traditional Bosnian coffee isn’t just about the drink, it’s about slowing down, taking your time and enjoying the moment. ⁠
⁠
And sometimes, that means a cigar and a box of matches served right alongside it.⁠
Because here, coffee is never just coffee. ⁠
🎥: @creatoremir

In Matera, Italy, you can spend the night inside a cave that people have lived in for centuries.⁠
⁠
Sextantio Le Grotte della Civita sits in the Sassi, one of the oldest inhabited areas in Italy and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. ⁠
⁠
Its 18 cave rooms were carefully restored to keep their original stone walls and arches, and guests can even enjoy candlelit dinners inside a former rock-cut church.⁠ 🕯️⁠
⁠
Would you spend a night here?⁠
⁠
By: @sextantio

Straight out of the ocean and onto the dance floor. 💃🌊⁠
Meet the Spanish dancer, a striking sea slug known for its vibrant red-orange color and graceful swimming style. ⁠
As it moves through the water, its wide body ripples like a flowing flamenco dress and that’s exactly where its name comes from.⁠
⁠
One of the ocean’s most unexpected performers. ❤️⁠
🎥: @hawaiiaquaman

Extreme heat is becoming a fact of life in more parts of the world, with serious implications for pregnant women and their babies.

Hundreds of studies have linked high heat exposure to adverse birth outcomes, but scientists are still trying to figure out just how hot is too hot. A recent study in Sydney is putting that question to the test, using a climate chamber that can reach 104°F (40°C) to determine when pregnant women can no longer safely regulate their core temperature. African dwarf crocodiles are among the smallest and least understood members of the crocodilian family. Across West and Central Africa, they are facing pressure from commercial hunting, deforestation, agriculture, and mining. Conservation ecologist and Rolex National Geographic Perpetual Planet Explorer Matt Shirley is developing new ways to study their populations and working with local hunters to explore more sustainable approaches to their harvest.
